name: IL-16
label: Safe R

key_factors: Republican-leaning district (R+11 PVI) with incumbent Darin LaHood running
Overwhelming financial edge: LaHood has $6.7M on hand vs. $230K for Nolley
Prediction markets price LaHood at roughly 96% to win
No polling or expert ratings, so the forecast rests on fundamentals
model.rationale: LaHood combines incumbency, a strongly Republican-leaning seat, and a roughly 15-to-1 cash advantage, while markets price his reelection near certainty. Nolley's minimal fundraising gives little evidence of a serious challenge, so the forecast sits at a double-digit Republican margin.
model.watch: A late surge of Democratic outside spending or an unexpected scandal could move this, but there is currently no sign of either.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Darin LaHood seeks another term in a central Illinois district that leans Republican by about eleven points. He is a well-established incumbent with no notable primary disruption and a large war chest, having raised $3.7 million and holding $6.7 million on hand. Challenger Paul Nolley has raised about $416,000 with $230,000 remaining, and no outside groups are meaningfully engaged on either side.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the picture rests on fundamentals and markets, which price LaHood around 96 percent. With a favorable district, incumbency, and a dominant money advantage, LaHood is a strong favorite, though the absence of polling keeps some uncertainty in the estimate.
